text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributes 0.75 to each of 4 members but only 1 if kept private, making full defection individually dominant even though full cooperation maximizes group welfare. I'm weighing pure self-interest against building cooperation, leaning toward a moderate contribution rather than either extreme.

This is a public goods game where each token contributed to the group gets multiplied by 0.75 and split among all 4 members. So contributing costs me 1 but only returns 0.75 to myself, a net loss of 0.25 individually, while the other three members gain 0.75 each — meaning contributing is personally costly but socially beneficial for the group overall.

Since full contribution maximizes group welfare, I'll open with cooperation by contributing all 20 tokens, then adjust my strategy based on how others respond.
